facts.fact: UNICEF says Nigeria's electronic birth registration, signed under a January 2025 compact with the NPC, NIMC and others, has interoperability between birth records, health information systems and the National Identification Number as a key feature.
UNICEF's June 2026 brief reports results of the Demographic and Health Survey 2023-2024 for Nigeria, the latest endorsed source for SDG 16.9.1.
UNICEF says electronic birth registration is embedded in routine health care and operational in 14 states and the Federal Capital Territory, driving towards national coverage.

NGA.note: Mentions Nigeria's digital strategy only in passing; no named strategy, standing or text.
No count or share of people holding a national ID.

facts.fact: UNICEF says the electronic birth registration initiative aims to link birth records with the National Identification Number so every child gets a verifiable legal identity from birth.

NGA.note: Nothing on who operates or owns the ID system.
No public register keyed on the ID number is stated.
Nothing on the national ID system's status, biometrics or certification.
Nothing on local government office connections.

facts.fact: UNICEF says frontline health workers and community birth attendants use digital tools to register births at the point of care, now operational in 14 states and the FCT.
